anti_generic_signature_read: Round one, unprimed, from the two orthographic ladder frames: "They vary, and the variation is clearly deliberate." It measured all eight globes across the row and then found the control itself: "the discs underneath do not vary -- disc 1 spans 240 px, disc 8 spans 235 px -- so the size difference is designed into the bodies alone, and the pieces are ordered largest-to-smallest along the row." It also found the Jupiter mirror cold, at the matched-camera frames, before knowing anybody had done anything to that world: "Two different objects. Confidence high. I would notice this swap."
blind_action_read: Round one, unprimed: "a person takes their eight-or-so planet pieces out of their tray, sets them on the grid, moves them across terrain of varying cost, and removes the opponent's." It named what it had worked that out from without being asked: "the disc-colour pairing, the three-stage board sequence in frame 17, the trays with piece-shaped recesses, and the differentiated cell faces -- not from any text, because the only text anywhere is a glyph about 40x85 px on each disc rim which is too small and too low-contrast for me to read in any frame."
blind_form_read: Round one, unprimed, counting geometric kinds rather than themes, it found eight: a sphere flattened at the bottom, mildly oblate on the large bodies and round on the small ones ("frame 05 left measures 355 px wide x 322 px tall (aspect 0.91)... frame 18's Earth measures 200 x 200 and frame 16's Venus 204 x 203 -- round. So the flattening is applied only to the big bodies"); a short truncated cone under each sphere; a low right cylinder base disc with a rounded top edge; a wide flat annular ring passing through one sphere at a tilt; a narrow near-vertical ring on another; slender cones of height about 2.6x their base diameter; flat square plates; and a raised square slab standing about 1.4x the plate thickness. It measured the base disc wall at "about 0.13 x diameter".
blind_held_read: Round one, unprimed, told only eighteen meaningless file names: "It is a two-player board game whose playing pieces are planets." It reached that from the object rather than from a label: "every piece stands on a flat circular disc, and those discs come in exactly two colours -- white and black -- and the same planet appears on both", plus "frame 17 shows the same board three times with progressively fewer pieces on it: I count roughly 14 pieces on the left board, 10 on the centre board, 5 on the right board. Pieces leave the board as play proceeds, so there is capture or removal." It read the terrain unprompted -- plain grey cells, brown cells with raised bumps, cyan and orange cells with radiating engraved lines, and two 2x2 groups each of a raised slab carrying two cones with three ray-engraved tiles around it -- and called it "terrain that modifies movement or scoring". It did not name Dou Shou Qi cold and is not recorded as having done so.
blind_relationship_read: Round one, unprimed: "Two things tell me it is two-player and not a display set. First, every piece stands on a flat circular disc, and those discs come in exactly two colours -- white and black -- and the same planet appears on both (frames 04, 05, 06, 07, 09, 12, 14, 16, 18 each show one white-based and one black-based copy)." It also read the two 2x2 terrain groups as one per colourway, and counted the trays as one per player with "8 or 10 slots per tray. If it is 8, that matches exactly eight planets per player."
blind_subjects_read: Round one, unprimed, it named the pieces as planets from their surfaces alone and, across the pair frames, distinguished nine distinct designs: a gold banded body with a red oval; a brown-and-grey banded body; a ringed body with a wide flat washer; a cyan body with a near-vertical ring; a blue body with three white stripe arcs and a grey oval; a blue-green body with green land masses; a pale yellow body with a single white band; a red body with a white polar cap; and a grey body with an orange annulus round a white centre. In round three, disclosed, it confirmed all eight are "each individually identifiable without a label".

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round one, unprimed, on the two matched-camera frames: "Two different objects. Confidence high. I would notice this swap." Its measurement: "the red spot is at (443,552) in frame 03 -- offset (-9,+192) from sphere centre (452,360), i.e. essentially on the centre meridian -- and at (598,518) in frame 10 -- offset (+146,+158). That is a 155-px horizontal difference against a 322-px horizontal radius: 0.48r, about 29 degrees of longitude, plus 34 px of latitude." Silhouettes identical at 645x598 px in both, so parallax is not available as an explanation. Confirmed a second parallax-free way in round three from the two orthographic ladder frames, where Jupiter's spot sits 37 px apart on an 85-px radius.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Jupiter's two pieces must read as two DIFFERENT objects, where before this revision they read as one piece photographed twice.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three, measured from pixels with one scale factor: the spot is 75 px long in frame 03 and the centre-to-centre travel is 154 px, so "154 / 75 = 2.05 spot-lengths. The design says about two. That is a match I did not have to reach for." Converted independently: "Delta-lambda = 30.7 degrees, +/-3" against the design's 28.46, and 6.70 mm of surface travel against the design's 6.20 mm, both inside its stated error. A third route from the orthographic ladders gave 33 degrees +/-6.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The mirror must be VISIBLE ACROSS A TABLE and not a rounding error: the design claims the Great Red Spot moves about two of its own lengths between the two pieces.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three: the red oval spans 75 px in frame 03 = 3.14 mm against the design's 3.06 mm, agreeing to 3%. It then checked that the two are one feature rather than two decals: "the frame-10 spot sits 144 px right of the sphere centre on a 322-px horizontal semi-axis, so sin = 0.447, cos = 0.894, and 75 x 0.894 = 67 px predicted against 67 measured. The two spots are the same painted feature seen at two longitudes."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The spot must still read as Jupiter's spot: one oval, the same size, at the same latitude band.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three read all eleven band boundaries down the centre meridian on both pieces -- the meridian a longitude reflection leaves invariant, which the critic derived itself as the right place to test -- and found the "largest disagreement anywhere: 5 px, on a vertical semi-axis of 299 px, which is 0.96 degrees of latitude. Every one of the eleven boundaries agrees within my reading error." Its round-two claim that the spot's own latitude had moved 5 degrees was withdrawn in round four against measure/jupiter-mirror.md's 0.00e+00 over 14 rings and 308 vertices.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: No LATITUDE may have moved: the six belts, the five bright zones and the Great Red Spot must sit at the same latitudes on both pieces.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three, belt widths down the centre meridian: "frame 03: 35, 42, 80, 68, 23, 13. Frame 10: 34, 43, 83, 65, 25, 15. Piece-to-piece agreement is within 3 px on every belt. All six widths are different from each other on both pieces... No two belts read as mirror images of one another: belts 3 and 4 are the two widest and their waves run differently." Six belts counted on both hemispheres of both armies.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: No belt may have changed width, and no two belts may have become mirror images of each other.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three: "if someone had 'fixed' the mirror by inventing a lean, the difference would have to be tens of degrees to show... I measured one band edge at both limbs in both frames: frame 03, a rise of 22 px = 2.05 degrees; frame 10, 15 px = 1.4 degrees. The differential between the two pieces is 0.6 degrees, not 6.26. Nothing like an invented lean is present in the image plane." It said plainly that a picture cannot confirm the 3.13 degree figure itself and named the model as the instrument for that.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The fix must NOT have been to invent a lean for Jupiter.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three: the Sol spot's offset from its own sphere centre is (-9, +192) on a 322-px horizontal semi-axis, i.e. "essentially on the centre meridian", which is where this frame's camera was solved to put it. The critic was explicit that a picture has no predecessor and named a geometry hash as the honest instrument; measure/revision-part-hashes.md carries part_world_jupiter_sol.step as byte-identical to the published set.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The Sol Jupiter must not have changed: its spot must still sit square to the camera at the frame named for it.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three, correcting its own unprimed round-one reading: "The x-offsets reverse sign on both off-meridian patches, which is the mirror. In round one I paired the Sol piece's upper-right patch with the Anti-Sol piece's right-hand patch -- matching by where they sat in the frame -- and concluded nothing had moved." Better still, the residuals were systematic: "All three are shifted about +9 px in x, in the same direction -- which is precisely the parallax I should expect... Subtract that common-mode +9 px and the mirror is exact to within 2 px on all three features."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Mercury's map must still be mirrored on the Anti-Sol piece.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three, at a matched +/-60 px baseline either side of each piece's own centre: "on the Sol piece... it rises 18 px left to right. On the Anti-Sol piece... it falls 25 px left to right. The slope reverses sign, which is what a reflection does to a monotonic feature." In round one it had called this frame not decidable, and said so: "Measuring it properly at a fixed baseline, I now do trust it."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Venus's map must still be mirrored on the Anti-Sol piece.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three counted them on both pieces of the pair frame and gave the pixel span of each: three white arcs plus the grey oval spot on the Sol piece, three white arcs plus the grey oval spot on the Anti-Sol piece. "Three bands and a spot on both."
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Neptune must still carry three white latitude bands and its dark spot.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three: "Both globes are uniform cyan apart from a smooth shading gradient; I looked specifically for a lighter pole, a hood, or any band edge and there is none. One near-vertical white ring on each." Corroborated in the two orthographic ladder frames and twice in the whole-set hero frame.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: Uranus must still be a bare globe with a white ring and no band, cap or hood.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three inspected all six corona cells corner by corner across two frames and gave the unbroken top-face outline of each: "Engraved sunburst only... Its far edge runs unbroken from (175,330) to (330,372). Nothing breaks the top-face outline anywhere." And: "Six corona cells inspected across two frames. Not one of them carries anything proud of its top face." In round one, before it knew what a trap was, it had already put the sunburst in a separate list of things cut INTO a surface.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: NO raised feature of any kind may stand above a trap tile's top face: not a horn, not a boss, not a pip, not a lip.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three: "the cones stand on the den, not on the traps", with each flame's base ellipse and tip measured on both stars, and nothing else raised anywhere on the field. Round one's unprimed list of everything standing above the playing surface contains the pieces, their discs and stems, the two rings, the belt-cell bumps, the raised den slab and the four cones -- and no trap tile.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The star's two flames must be unchanged and must be the ONLY raised flames on the board.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round one, unprimed, from the two orthographic ladder frames: "They vary, and the variation is clearly deliberate... the discs underneath do not vary -- disc 1 spans 240 px, disc 8 spans 235 px -- so the size difference is designed into the bodies alone, and the pieces are ordered largest-to-smallest along the row." In round four it re-derived the ladder from the fifth-root rule and one anchor, reproduced the design's own figures exactly, and found "four classes of two, separated by 15.3%, 23.7% and 11.0% -- large, obvious steps", withdrawing the round-three reading it had built on mis-measured pixels.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: All eight globes must be comparable at one scale so that rank is something a reader can SEE.

critical_form_requirements.blind_evidence: Round three counted each: "frame 11 shows 8 on white discs, frame 08 shows 8 on black. Widths descend 170, 170, 155, 165, 135, 145, 125, 105 px while the discs stay constant at 235-240 px, so rank is carried by the globe." Six corona cells, 3 orange and 3 cyan; two stars; two trays; twelve belt tiles in two blocks of six. It said the four board panels' seams are not resolvable at this scale rather than claiming them.
critical_form_requirements.requirement: The set must still be Dou Shou Qi with eight ranked worlds per side, twelve belt tiles, six corona cells, two stars and two orbit trays.

largest_risk: The critic's own corrected wording, round four, replacing the round-three version it withdrew after re-deriving the ladder and finding its own pixel readings had inverted two pairs: "Rank resolves cleanly into four size-classes separated by 11-24%, and which world you are holding is never in doubt. Within a class, size cannot order the pair: Uranus and Neptune differ by 0.13 mm and Earth and Venus by 0.17 mm. Uranus versus Neptune is the one ordering a player must learn rather than see, and the disc numeral that exists to settle it is the thing I was never able to read." It then deflated its own risk unprompted: the numeral is about 1.7 by 3.5 mm on the real part, "certainly not readable across a table, but a 3.5 mm engraved numeral is plausibly readable in the hand -- and you pick a piece up to move it, which is exactly when a Uranus/Neptune question arises." A second observation is carried open and explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this revision: at the pair frames the critic could measure the mirrored lean on Mars and Saturn but not on Earth, Neptune or Uranus, and it named reading the sixteen signed obliquities from the model as the cheapest thing that would settle it.
resolution: ONE independent critic, FOUR rounds, ZERO geometry repairs: no CAD changed at any point, so the images read blind in round one are the images sealed here. Round one was unprimed on 18 frames copied to meaningless names in a shuffled order, balanced 14 whole-object-and-pair against 4 Jupiter detail frames, with both orthographic rank-ladder frames in the set. Rounds two, three and four were disclosed comparisons against those same frozen pictures and none is claimed as a naive reading. The critic filed eight defects cold and ALL EIGHT were retired: four by its own re-measurement in round two (a lighting difference it had read as a second paint scheme, a feature-matching error on Mercury, a shadowless renderer it had read as floating trays, and a far-face placement complaint), and four by deterministic gates in round three (interference 0 clashes over 220 occurrences and 413 tested pairs; ring 15.00 mm radius inside a 17.00 mm disc inside an 18.00 mm half-cell; 0.292 mm of flame-base edge clearance reproduced from the constants by the critic itself, plus a passing overhang gate; and the single-solid build assert). It also withdrew a round-two finding of its own -- that the spot's latitude had moved 5 degrees -- against a 308-vertex measurement of exactly 0.00e+00, and named the weak camera-elevation estimate that had produced it. A self-citation check ran in both directions: the critic found three of eight quotations in the Manager's record inaccurate and supplied corrected text, which is what this record uses.
reviewer: One independent native critic. Round 1 unprimed on 18 name-blind canonical renders; rounds 2-4 disclosed re-reviews on the same frozen images. No geometry changed between rounds.
